Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 22 (Bu-Vb Sk22), titled *Dutiyakhambhakata* ("Hands on hips"), is an etiquette training rule (*sekhiya*) for Buddhist monastics preserved in the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text belongs to the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga and regulates monastic deportment, specifically addressing the training not to sit with hands placed on the hips in inhabited areas [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule has been published by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral identifies a comprehensive network of parallels across early Buddhist Vinaya lineages [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali tradition, it corresponds directly to the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bu-pm-sk22*), the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (*pli-tv-bi-vb-sk22*), the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bi-pm-sk22*), and both the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Parivāra Sekhiya 22 [SuttaCentral]. Parallels outside the Theravāda tradition are preserved across multiple Vinaya schools in Sanskrit and Chinese, including the Sarvāstivāda (e.g., *Lzh Sarv Bu Vb Sk36*, *san-sarv-bu-pm-tf11-sk34*), Dharmaguptaka (*Lzh Dg Bu Vb Sk 13* and Bhikkhunī parallels), Mahāsāṅghika (*Lzh Mg Bu Vb Sk22*, *san-mg-bu-pm-sk22*), Mahīśāsaka (*lzh-mi-bu-vb-sk30*), and Lokottaravāda (*san-lo-bu-pm-sk22*, *san-lo-bi-vb-sk22*) [SuttaCentral].

Internal text-reuse data computed by DharmaNexus demonstrates 119 matching passages across 42 Pali texts, driven by the uniform phraseology characteristic of the Sekhiya rules [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches in DharmaNexus met the score threshold of 10 [DharmaNexus].
